title: Animation Energy Transfer Studio
description: Three objects orbit a central stage: an animated box, sunglasses, and a shader ball. The user distributes a fixed pool of 100 animation energy units among the three objects using sliders and click-drag transfers, controlling rotation speed, bounce amplitude, and color-cycle rate respectively. Energy is conserved — boosting one object drains others — and a full undo/redo history lets the user rewind any allocation step.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads BoxAnimated.glb, SunglassesKhronos.glb, and ShaderBall2.glb via GLTFLoader. Place all three models on a circular platform (radius 4) at 120-degree intervals, each on a small pedestal. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0,5,10) looking at origin, with OrbitControls. Add ambient light (0.4) and two directional lights from opposite sides.

Core mechanic — Energy Conservation: maintain a total energy pool of exactly 100 units split among three channels: Box rotation speed (0-100), Sunglasses bounce amplitude (0-100), ShaderBall color-cycle rate (0-100). The sum must always equal 100. Display three vertical sliders in an HTML overlay panel on the left. When the user drags one slider up, the other two decrease proportionally to conserve the total. Show numeric readouts beside each slider and a total counter that always reads 100.

Animation mapping: BoxAnimated plays its built-in animation with timeScale proportional to its energy (0 energy = paused, 100 = 4x speed). Sunglasses bounce vertically using sin(time) with amplitude mapped from energy (0 = still, 100 = 2 units). ShaderBall cycles its material color through an HSL hue rotation at a rate mapped from its energy (0 = static, 100 = fast rainbow).

Drag transfer: the user can click one object, drag to another, releasing to transfer 10 energy units from source to target (clamped to available). Highlight the source green and target yellow during drag, drawing a glowing line between them.

Undo/Redo: maintain a history stack of energy states (max 50). Keyboard Z = undo, Y = redo. Show undo/redo buttons in the UI panel with step count. Each slider change or drag transfer pushes a new state.

Multi-input coupling: holding Shift while dragging a slider locks the other two sliders to equal split of remaining energy instead of proportional. This creates a second interaction mode.

Add a reset button that animates all values back to 33/33/34 over 0.5 seconds. Display a small bar chart beside the sliders showing real-time energy distribution. Use requestAnimationFrame for the render loop.
